changes nothing. Errors go to stderr with a nonzero exit.

## Sessions and machines

- `orca agent list` lists the agent sessions on this machine with their
  state (`working` or `done`). Your own session has `"self": true`.
- `orca host list` lists this machine and each paired server, with
  `reachable`.
- `orca repo list` lists the repositories Orca knows.
- `orca worktree list` lists worktrees with their comments.
  `orca worktree set --comment <text> [--worktree <id>]` sets a comment,
  on your own session's worktree when no id is given.
  `orca worktree rm <id>` removes one that no working worker uses.

  creates a child Run that a worker can start its own workers in.
- `orca orchestration worker-list` and `orca orchestration worker-show <id>`

## Workers

- `orca orchestration worker-start --agent <claude|codex> --model <model>
  (--environment local | --on <host>) (--brief <text> | --brief-file <path>)

  open after it finishes.

  creates a child Run that a worker can start its own workers in.
- `orca orchestration worker-list` and `orca orchestration worker-show <id>`
  report each worker's state, worktree, pull request, parent, and whether it
  sent `worker_done`.
- Worker states: `working`, `exited` (stopped on its own), `stopped`,

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Stand-in for the GitHub CLI, used only by the reviewing-prs and repo-captain Skill Evals.

The Eval Cases need the skill to run its real discovery, read, and write
commands. Handing an agent files and telling it they came from GitHub would
test a different program than the one that ships, so this stand-in sits where
`gh` would be on PATH and answers from one synthetic world. It never contacts
GitHub.

Reads are answered from the world. The few writes the skills make (comment,
label, merge, a pull request, an issue edit, issue scores) are applied to a
private state copy and recorded in a trace. Everything else is refused with a
nonzero exit, so a run that strays fails loudly instead of passing on silence.

A world may change between operator turns. The runner writes the turn number
to `turn` in the state directory before sending that turn; the changes the
world lists under `turns` up to that number are then applied once, and a pull
request waiting in a repository's merge queue leaves it, merged or ejected.

Environment:
  GH_STANDIN_WORLD  path to a fixture's world.json (never written)
  GH_STANDIN_STATE  existing directory outside any git work tree; holds
                    state.json, trace.jsonl, and the optional turn file

Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 an error GitHub or gh would return, 3 outside this
stand-in's contract, 4 not configured or unsafe paths.
"""

The main reason is that this repo isn't set up the way the coordinating-work skill expects, so the skill gives me no authority to merge. ## Why I didn't act

- **The setup is different.** The record (in `xdg-state/ledger-app-captain/`) describes an older arrangement: a coordinator with two team leads under it, each starting its own workers. Both leads (w-1 invoices, w-2 docs) have no recorded parent, so this skill treats them as separate team leads. I can only act on their messages for things I could decide alone, and merging isn't one of them.
- **No approved merge rules.** The charter says "Merge the routine PRs yourself. Hold everything else for my review round." That's a real approval, but there's no approved proposal defining what counts as merge-ready, and the skill says to merge nothing without one.
- **I couldn't read mail without consuming it.** Orca's guide offers no way to read messages without marking them read. So I didn't read w-4's done-message or anything else waiting.

## Problems

1. **#565 and #566 are closed, but the work isn't on main.** The docs lead's notes say both merged. But no PR exists for either, `docs/plans.md` and `docs/accounts.md` aren't on `origin/main`, and w-5 (on #566) has no PR. I recommend reopening both. Reopening is a tracker write your approval would cover, and this setup's `gh` can't reopen issues anyway.

I'd arm nothing. This skill only allows a periodic check once a setup has been approved, and none has.
